title: Extract the email addresses of all employees and return as a comma-separated string using `Collectors.joining(", ")`.
shortTitle: Extract the email addresses of all employees and return as a comma-separated string using Collectors.joining(", ")
keyPoints: Collectors.joining(delimiter) concatenates a stream of strings into one string with the given delimiter
The three-argument joining(delimiter, prefix, suffix) wraps the result, useful for bracketed lists
joining() uses a StringJoiner internally, appending to one buffer for O(n) performance
joining only works on Stream<CharSequence>; map to strings first before collecting
A null element in the stream throws NullPointerException during concatenation
No delimiter is placed before the first element or after the last element

s1_definition.oneliner: `Collectors.joining(", ")` glues a stream of strings into one comma-separated string.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **`Collectors.joining(delimiter)`** concatenates a stream of strings with the given separator between each pair.
- **Three overloads**: no-arg (plain concat), one-arg (delimiter), three-arg (delimiter, prefix, suffix).
- **Internally uses `StringJoiner`**, which appends to a single buffer for O(n) performance.
- **No trailing delimiter**: the separator appears only between elements, not at the start or end.
- **Requires `Stream<CharSequence>`**: you must map to strings first.
s1_definition.analogy: The office manager at the National Bank of India wants to send one email to all staff, so she needs every address strung together, separated by commas, to paste into the To box. `joining(", ")` is exactly that stringing-together.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Stream<Employee>
  [Rajesh, Priya, Amit]
       │
       │  .map(Employee::getEmail)
       ▼
  Stream<String>
  ["rajesh@nbi.com", "priya@nbi.com", "amit@nbi.com"]
       │
       │  .collect(Collectors.joining(", "))
       │
       │  StringJoiner buffer:
       │  "rajesh@nbi.com"
       │  "rajesh@nbi.com, priya@nbi.com"
       │  "rajesh@nbi.com, priya@nbi.com, amit@nbi.com"
       ▼
  String: "rajesh@nbi.com, priya@nbi.com, amit@nbi.com"
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
To turn a stream of strings into one delimited string I use the joining collector, giving it the delimiter I want between elements. Here I first mapped each employee to its email, then collected with `joining(", ")`, which concatenates all the addresses with a comma and space between each, and no delimiter before the first or after the last.

In my banking project at the National Bank of India this built the recipient line for a staff circular, where the office manager needed every address in one comma-separated string. The three-argument form with prefix and suffix is handy for building a bracketed summary.

joining uses a StringJoiner internally, so it appends to one growing buffer for O(n) performance, unlike reduce with string concatenation which is O(n^2). A null in the stream throws NullPointerException, so I always filter nulls before joining.

Remember one sentence: `Collectors.joining(", ")` concatenates a stream of strings efficiently using a StringJoiner, with the delimiter only between elements.
